cards.prose: The parable he is about to tell is a feast, and Isaiah had already set the table: *a feast of fat things* on the mountain of Yahuah (the LORD). The king's dinner, *my oxen and my fatlings are killed* (Matthew 22:4), is that same table, ready and waiting for whoever comes.
cards.member_phrase: in this mountain shall Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) make unto all people a feast of fat things
cards.member_sentence: The feast is Yahuah's (the LORD's) own, spread on his mountain, and the king's dinner in the parable is that table made ready.

cards.prose: The parable is an invitation, and Isaiah's cry is the same one: *come ye*, and *buy wine and milk without money and without price*. The table costs the guest nothing, but it still has a host who sent the call, and the parable is about what the bidden did with it.
cards.member_phrase: come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's open call to the thirsty, with no money asked, is the invitation the king's servants carry out in the parable.

cards.prose: Isaiah has the clothing before the parable does. Yahuah (the LORD) *hath clothed me with the garments of salvation*, and the figure he uses is a bridegroom and a bride dressed for their day. A wedding has its own dress, and the story Yahusha (Jesus) is starting will come back to it.
cards.member_phrase: he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's garments of salvation and robe of righteousness, worn by bridegroom and bride, are the wedding dress the parable has in view.

cards.prose: The parable's wedding is the one Revelation shouts over: *Alleluia: for Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) omnipotent reigneth*, and the next verse says *the marriage of the Lamb is come* (Revelation 19:7). The king who made a marriage for his son and the Lamb whose marriage has come are the same feast seen from the far end.
cards.member_phrase: saying, Alleluia: for Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) omnipotent reigneth
cards.member_sentence: The multitude shouts that Yahuah (the LORD) reigns, and the next verse names the marriage of the Lamb that the parable's wedding looks toward.

cards.prose: The king burns the city of the men who slew his servants, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the same in plain words a chapter later: Jerusalem, *thou that killest the prophets* (Matthew 23:37), has its house left *desolate*. It is the house that is emptied, the temple and its rule, and in the same breath he speaks of gathering her children.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The burned city of the parable is said plainly here: the house is left desolate, spoken to the city that kills the prophets.

cards.prose: The parable burns a city, and two chapters on Yahusha (Jesus) walks out of the temple while the disciples point him to its buildings. His answer is that *There shall not be left here one stone upon another* (Matthew 24:2), the burned city of the parable said again at the temple's own door.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He leaves the temple and the disciples show him its buildings, which sets up what he says next about the stones.
cards.flag: Target is only the opening verse of the scene; the point of the pair rests on the verse after it, quoted in the prose.

cards.prose: Jeremiah 7 is where this was first spoken. The word came to him at the gate of the house, to a people leaning on the building: *Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 7:4). The king's burned city is what that word warned of.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The word to Jeremiah at the gate of the house, against trusting the temple, is the older warning behind the burned city.
cards.flag: Target verse is only the opening line of Jeremiah 7; the prose leans on 7:4 from the context.

cards.prose: The king sends *his armies* against those who killed his servants, and Isaiah shows Yahuah (the LORD) doing the same before: *O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger*. The army is his rod, taken up against a people that had earned it, and the one who wields it is the one who was wronged.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) has sent an army as his rod of anger before, and the king's armies in the parable are sent the same way.

cards.prose: The king looks for *a wedding garment* and finds a guest without one. Isaiah says what that clothing is: Yahuah (the LORD) *hath clothed me with the garments of salvation*, with *the robe of righteousness*. The guest has come in at the door, and what is missing is what he is wearing.
cards.member_phrase: he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness
cards.member_sentence: The robe of righteousness that Yahuah (the LORD) puts on his people is what the king looks for on the guest and does not find.

cards.prose: Isaiah's people stand in *filthy rags*, their iniquities having *taken us away*, yet the same prayer says Yahuah (the LORD) *meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness* (Isaiah 64:5). The man at the feast has the rags and not the righteousness the king looks for.
cards.member_phrase: we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah's confession of filthy rags and of iniquities that carried the people away is what the man at the feast is standing in.

cards.prose: Joshua the high priest stands before the angel of Yahuah (the LORD) in *filthy garments*, and the word is *I will clothe thee with change of raiment* (Zechariah 3:4). The man at the feast has not had that change, and the king sees it the moment he comes in.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Joshua's filthy garments, taken off and exchanged for clean raiment, show the change of clothing that the guest at the feast lacks.

cards.prose: Revelation names the garment: *fine linen, clean and white*, and *the fine linen is the righteousness of saints*. It is granted to the wife at the marriage, so a guest in other clothes stands out the moment the king comes in to look.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The wedding garment is named here: fine linen, clean and white, which is the righteousness of saints.

cards.prose: To Sardis the word is that a few *have not defiled their garments* (Revelation 3:4), and the one who overcomes *shall be clothed in white raiment*. The guest in the parable was called and came in, and what he lacked was this clothing, which comes with the promise that the name of the one who wears it is not blotted out.
cards.member_phrase: He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life
cards.member_sentence: White raiment is given to the one who overcomes, and his name is kept in the book of life, which is the clothing the guest lacked.

cards.prose: The man at the feast was bidden and came through the door, and he is cast out all the same, which is what *Not every one that saith unto me* means. What decides it in both places is the doing, *he that doeth the will of my Father*, and the garment is what that doing looks like when the king comes to see.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Saying the word is not enough to enter, and the one who does the will of the Father enters, the same test the garment sets at the feast.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) closes the labourers in the vineyard and the wedding feast with the same sentence. In both the call goes out wide, and in both what he counts at the end is the chosen, not the called. *Many be called, but few chosen* is said twice, over two different tables.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The same closing sentence ends the labourers in the vineyard, where the call goes wide and the chosen are the few.

cards.prose: Isaiah is sent to a people who *Hear ye indeed, but understand not*. The call in the parable goes out as wide as that, and what separates the chosen from the called is not made by the hearing. Those who understand were his before they heard, and the hearing brings that out.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The word to Isaiah, to a people that hear and do not understand, shows why many are called and few are chosen.

cards.prose: In Revelation the ones with the Lamb when he overcomes are *called, and chosen, and faithful*, three words where Matthew gives two. The few of the parable are the ones counted there, and the guest without the garment shows what it looks like to be called and not faithful.
cards.member_phrase: they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful
cards.member_sentence: Those with the Lamb when he overcomes are called, and chosen, and faithful, the few that the parable's closing sentence counts.

cards.prose: He asks whose image is on the coin, and it is Caesar's, so the coin goes to Caesar. Genesis has another image in view: *Let us make man in our image, after our likeness*. The one who carries that image belongs to Elohim (God), which is what his answer leaves them to see.
cards.member_phrase: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness
cards.member_sentence: Man is made in Elohim's (God's) image, so the one stamped with it is what Yahusha (Jesus) says belongs to Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Romans stands on the same ground as the coin: Caesar has real things, and they are his because *the powers that be are ordained of Elohim (God)*. The power is set under the one who ordained it, so what Caesar is owed is measured by whose he is.
cards.member_phrase: For there is no power but of Elohim (God): the powers that be are ordained of Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Rulers hold their power from Elohim (God), so Caesar's things are Caesar's under him and never apart from him.

cards.prose: Peter writes to *strangers and pilgrims* (1 Peter 2:11), people living under rulers that are not their own, and he gives them the coin's answer: *every ordinance of man*, even *to the king, as supreme*. The reason he gives is Yahusha's (Jesus's) sake, not the ruler's strength.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Peter tells strangers and pilgrims to honour the ordinances of men, even the king as supreme, which is the coin's answer carried to people under rulers not their own.

cards.prose: The coin has two owners, and Peter stands where the two claims part. The council has just forbidden the apostles to teach in his name, and his answer is *We ought to obey Elohim (God) rather than men*. A command that reaches past what is Caesar's into what is Elohim's (God's) ends there.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Where a command from men reaches past what belongs to them, the apostles answer that Elohim (God) is obeyed first.

cards.prose: The riddle is built on a commandment of Moses: when a brother dies without a child, his brother *shall go in unto her* and carry the dead man's name forward. The law is Moses', and the Sadducees take it and set it against the resurrection, as if a duty to a dead man's line could make the dead rising look absurd.
cards.member_phrase: shall go in unto her, and take her to him to wife
cards.member_sentence: The commandment for a brother to raise up a child for the one who died is the law the Sadducees' seven brothers are built on.

cards.prose: The Sadducees treat the brother's duty as a puzzle, but Genesis 38 opens Yahudah's (Judah's) household, with its sons Er and Onan, and it is there that the duty to a childless widow is first seen at work. The seed was carried forward by the brother, which is what the seven brothers in the riddle are supposed to be doing.
cards.member_phrase: Yahudah (Judah) went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite
cards.member_sentence: Genesis 38 opens Yahudah's (Judah's) household, where a brother's duty to a childless widow was already at work long before Moses.
cards.flag: Target is only the first verse of Genesis 38; the levirate story itself is in later verses of the chapter.

cards.prose: Boaz goes up to the gate and sits the nearer kinsman down before ten elders to settle Elimelech's land. It is the brother's duty carried out in the open, with a widow's family at stake, and not turned into a riddle to trap someone.
cards.member_phrase: went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there
cards.member_sentence: Boaz settles the right of the nearer kinsman at the gate before ten elders, the same family duty the Sadducees turn into a riddle.
cards.flag: Target is only the opening verse of Ruth 4.

cards.prose: Acts says what the Sadducees hold: *no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit*. So the question brought to Yahusha (Jesus) is no puzzle they want solved but their own denial dressed as one, and his answer deals with the resurrection and with the angels.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Acts states the Sadducees' creed, no resurrection, angel or spirit, which is what their question about the seven brothers is really arguing.

cards.prose: He tells the Sadducees they err, *not knowing the scriptures*. To others he says *Search the scriptures*, for *they are they which testify of me*. The fault in both rooms is the same: the writings are in their hands and the one they point to is not seen.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He sends them to the scriptures, which testify of him, the same writings the Sadducees are told they do not know.

cards.prose: Timothy had *known the holy scriptures* from a child, and when he was a child those were Moses and the prophets. They are the writings Yahusha (Jesus) says the Sadducees do not know, and the ones he reasons from in the next breath.
cards.member_phrase: from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures
cards.member_sentence: The scriptures Timothy knew from a child, Moses and the prophets, are the writings the Sadducees are told they do not know.

cards.prose: The raised neither marry nor are given in marriage, and he sets them beside the angels in heaven. Genesis tells of other sons of Elohim (God) who did the opposite, for *they took them wives of all which they chose* (Genesis 6:2). The ones in heaven keep their place, and the ones in Genesis left it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Genesis 6 begins the account of the sons of Elohim (God) who took wives, the other side of the angels who stay in heaven.

cards.prose: Jude names angels who *kept not their first estate* and *left their own habitation*, held in chains for the judgment. The angels Yahusha (Jesus) points to are the ones who stayed in heaven, and the Sadducees' puzzle about marriage never touches the difference between the two.
cards.member_phrase: kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains
cards.member_sentence: Jude's angels left their own habitation and are held for judgment, the contrast to the angels in heaven the raised are likened to.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) puts the raised beside the angels of Elohim (God) in heaven, and Paul says of them *we shall judge angels*. The ones who stand beside the faithful angels are also the ones who sit over the angels that left their place.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The raised, likened to the angels in heaven, are also said to judge angels, the ones who left their place.

cards.prose: This is the verse he means by *that which was spoken unto you by Elohim (God)*. At the bush, long after the fathers had died, he says 'I am' their Elohim (God), not 'I was'. The resurrection is not written out in those words, and Yahusha (Jesus) reasons it from them, line upon line: if Elohim (God) is still theirs, they are not gone.
cards.member_phrase: I am the Elohim (God) of thy father, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob
cards.member_sentence: Elohim (God) at the bush still calls himself the Elohim (God) of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and Yahusha (Jesus) reasons the resurrection out of it.

cards.prose: The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, and Daniel wrote it down: *that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake*. The word is sleeping, not ending. It is the same thing Yahusha (Jesus) draws from the bush, said outright by the prophet.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Daniel says outright that many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to life and some to shame.

cards.prose: Isaiah says it as a promise about Yahuah's (the LORD's) own dead: *Thy dead men shall live*. Those who *dwell in dust* are told to *Awake and sing*, so the fathers the Sadducees count as finished are spoken of as sleepers who will rise.
cards.member_phrase: Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah promises that Yahuah's (the LORD's) dead shall live and those in the dust shall awake and sing.

cards.prose: The one who spoke at the bush says through Hosea what he will do with the dead: *I will ransom them from the power of the grave*. Elohim (God) is the living one who does the ransoming, so the fathers he still calls his own are not out of his reach.
cards.member_phrase: I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) says he will ransom his own from the power of the grave and redeem them from death.

cards.prose: Job, looking toward his own end, says *my redeemer liveth*, and that he *shall stand at the latter day upon the earth*. The living one standing over the dust has the last word over the dead, which is the thought the bush carries: Elohim (God) is the Elohim (God) of the living.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Job knows that his redeemer lives and will stand upon the earth at the latter day, the living one over the dead.

cards.prose: The Sadducees would have answered the question Ezekiel is asked in the valley, *Son of Adam, can these bones live?* (Ezekiel 37:3), with a no. Ezekiel answers, *thou knowest* (Ezekiel 37:3), and the word of Yahuah (the LORD) then goes out to the bones.
cards.member_phrase: set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel is set down in a valley of dry bones and asked whether they can live, the question the Sadducees answered with no.

cards.prose: David says his flesh *shall rest in hope*, which is the word of one who sleeps, not of one who ends. Two lines on he says what he hopes for, *Thou wilt not leave my soul in hell* (Psalm 16:10), so the one who rests is not forgotten there, and that is the same hope Yahusha (Jesus) finds at the bush.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: David's flesh rests in hope, and the next lines say his soul is not left in hell, the sleeper kept and not forgotten.

cards.prose: He answers the lawyer from the Shema, Moses' own opening to Yashar'el (Israel): *Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD)*, and the love he names follows in the next verse. Nothing in the answer is new to the lawyer, since these are the words every father in Yashar'el (Israel) was told to teach his children.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The first commandment is the Shema, which begins with who Yahuah (the LORD) is before it says to love him.

cards.prose: The second is from Moses too. It closes a verse about grudges and vengeance, *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself*, and carries the seal *I am Yahuah (LORD)*. Yahusha (Jesus) puts Deuteronomy and Leviticus side by side as one answer, and both are the law, not a way around it.
cards.member_phrase: but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD)
cards.member_sentence: The second commandment is Leviticus 19:18, love of the neighbour, set in the same law as the first and sealed with Yahuah's (the LORD's) name.

cards.prose: The neighbour in Leviticus 19 reaches further than the man next door. The stranger dwelling with them *shall be unto you as one born among you*, and the command is *love him as thyself*, with the reason given, *ye were strangers in the land of Egypt*.
cards.member_phrase: the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself
cards.member_sentence: The same law that says love the neighbour says it again of the stranger dwelling with them, as one born among them.

cards.prose: The love Yahusha (Jesus) names as first comes with its hands full: Moses writes *his statutes, and his judgments, and his commandments* in the same verse. Nothing in his answer lets the love stand in for the keeping.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Moses joins love of Yahuah (the LORD) to keeping his charge, statutes, judgments and commandments, in one verse.

cards.prose: The love he commands is something Yahuah (the LORD) promises to do in his people: he will *circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed* to love him. It is said to those he gathers back, *from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee* (Deuteronomy 30:4), so the command and the new heart come from the same hand.
cards.member_phrase: will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to circumcise the heart of his gathered people so that they love him, the command made possible by his own work.

cards.prose: Micah answers the question the lawyer asks, what is good and what is required, in a sentence: *do justly, and to love mercy*, and *walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)*. Loving Yahuah (the LORD) and loving the neighbour is that walk laid out, and the prophets say it as plainly as the law does.
cards.member_phrase: what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Micah says what Yahuah (the LORD) requires in one sentence, justice, mercy and a humble walk with Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Hosea gives the second commandment its edge: Yahuah (the LORD) says *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice*, and *the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings*. He is turning from sacrifice with no knowing of him behind it, and the knowing shows in how a man deals with his neighbour.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) wants mercy and the knowledge of Elohim (God) over sacrifice offered without them.

cards.prose: He said it at the close of the Sermon on the Mount and he says it again to the lawyer: all that you would have men do to you, do to them, *for this is the law and the prophets*. Twice the law and the prophets are said to rest on how a man treats his neighbour, and neither time are they taken away.
cards.member_phrase: for this is the law and the prophets
cards.member_sentence: The Golden Rule is given as the law and the prophets, the same weight the great commandment carries at the end of the chapter.

cards.prose: Paul says it too: *he that loveth another hath fulfilled the law*, and the next verse names the commandments love keeps, *Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not kill, Thou shalt not steal* (Romans 13:9). Love does not stand in for the law, and it is how the commandments get done.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul says loving another fulfils the law and then names the commandments, so love is how they are kept.

cards.prose: Paul writes to the Galatians that *all the law is fulfilled in one word*, and the word is the Leviticus line Yahusha (Jesus) gave as the second commandment. The whole law is still standing there to be fulfilled, and the sentence would say nothing if it were gone.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: In Galatians the whole law is fulfilled in the one word, love of the neighbour, the second commandment of the chapter.

cards.prose: James calls it *the royal law according to the scripture* and then quotes the Leviticus line. He says those who fulfil it *do well*, and in the next lines he goes on to the commandments against adultery and killing, so the law is still named and still being kept.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: James calls the neighbour commandment the royal law and treats it as the scripture's own word, still to be fulfilled.

cards.prose: At Jacob's well, wearied from the road, Yahusha (Jesus) asks a woman of Samaria for a drink, on the ground Jacob gave to his son Joseph. The second commandment is walked out there: he goes to one the Yahudim (Jews) had no dealings with and asks her for something, as a neighbour would.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: At the well he asks a woman of Samaria for a drink, the love of neighbour shown to one others kept away from.
cards.flag: The old note meant 1 John (love of Elohim and the brother), but the pair as it stands is the gospel of John; I wrote to the scene actually on the page, the woman of Samaria at Jacob's well, and did not re-point.

cards.prose: He goes up to Jerusalem at a feast of the Yahudim (Jews) and walks into the porches of Bethesda, where lay *a great multitude of impotent folk* (John 5:3). The two commandments are in one trip, the feast of Yahuah (the LORD) and the sick at the pool.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He goes up to Jerusalem for the feast and then to Bethesda, where the blind, lame and withered lay waiting.
cards.flag: The old note meant 1 John 5:3 (keeping his commandments is the love of Elohim), but the pair as it stands is John 5:2, the pool at Bethesda; I wrote to that scene and did not re-point.

cards.prose: He puts one verse of David to the Pharisees, and there are two in it: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks, and David calls the one spoken to *my Lord*. That one is seated at the right hand because he is told, *Sit thou at my right hand*. He is David's son and Elohim (God) with a Father, and the question is left standing.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) speaks to the one David bows to and seats him at his right hand, the verse Yahusha (Jesus) puts to the Pharisees.

cards.prose: Three verses on, the same psalm calls the one at the right hand a priest: Yahuah (the LORD) *hath sworn, and will not repent*, *a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek)*. The one David bows to is no mere heir to a throne. He is seated, sworn to, and a priest, which is more than the answer the Pharisees gave.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The same psalm swears the one at the right hand a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).

cards.prose: They answer that the Messiah (Christ) is *The Son of David* (Matthew 22:42), and Psalm 2 gives the other half: Yahuah (the LORD) says to the king he has set on Zion, *Thou art my Son*. Both are true of the one he is asking about, a son of David and a Son with a Father.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Psalm 2 has Yahuah (the LORD) call his king his Son, the half of the answer beside the Son of David.

cards.prose: The Pharisees gave the right first half: the Messiah (Christ) comes from David, *thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels*. Yahuah (the LORD) promised a son whose kingdom he would establish, and that is what the Pharisees held. The question Yahusha (Jesus) asks is whether that is all of him.
cards.member_phrase: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises David a son from his own body whose kingdom he will establish, the answer the Pharisees gave.

cards.prose: Isaiah's child is born *unto us*, a son given, and his names include El Gibbor (The mighty God). A son, and named Elohim (God): that is the riddle the Pharisees could not answer, how David's son is also the one David bows to.
cards.member_phrase: unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder
cards.member_sentence: The child born and the son given carries the government and the name El Gibbor (The mighty God), a son named Elohim (God).

cards.prose: The Pharisees knew where the answer began, *a rod out of the stem of Jesse*, and *a Branch shall grow out of his roots*. Isaiah goes on to say *the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him* (Isaiah 11:2), so the line of David has something in it more than David.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah has the Branch come from the stem of Jesse, David's own line, with the spirit of Yahuah (the LORD) resting on him.

cards.prose: Yahuah (the LORD) says through Jeremiah that he will *raise unto David a righteous Branch*, and that *a King shall reign and prosper*. It comes right after the promise to gather the remnant of his flock from all countries, so the son of David is the one who gathers as well as the one who reigns.
cards.member_phrase: I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) will raise up a righteous Branch for David, who reigns and executes judgment and justice in the earth.

cards.prose: The one David bows to sits at the right hand in the psalm, and in Daniel *one like the Son of Adam* comes with the clouds to the Ancient of days and is given a kingdom that *shall not pass away* (Daniel 7:14). Daniel's word is *like*: he saw one who looked like a son of Adam, the one who would take on flesh, brought near before the Father.
cards.member_phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam come with the clouds to the Ancient of days and receive an everlasting kingdom.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) answers the high priest with the two verses he laid before the Pharisees in the temple: the one *sitting on the right hand of power*, and the Son of Adam *coming in the clouds of heaven*. What he asked them as a riddle, he now says of himself.
cards.member_phrase: Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven
cards.member_sentence: Before the council he joins the right hand of power and the coming in the clouds, naming himself in what he asked the Pharisees.

cards.prose: Peter takes up the question Yahusha (Jesus) left hanging in the temple. David *is not ascended into the heavens*, so the one he calls *my Lord* is someone else, and Peter tells all the house of Yashar'el (Israel) who: *that same Yahusha (Jesus), whom ye have crucified* (Acts 2:36).
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Peter says David did not ascend, so the one at Yahuah's (the LORD's) right hand in the psalm is another, Yahusha (Jesus).

cards.prose: Hebrews says where the one David bowed to sits: *on the right hand of the Majesty on high*. He is *the brightness of his glory* and *the express image of his person*, the one who can be seen beside the one who cannot, seated after he had done what he came to do.
cards.member_phrase: sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high
cards.member_sentence: The Son, the brightness of the glory and the express image of his person, sits down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

cards.prose: The psalm is put to the angels as a question, and the answer is none. Elohim (God) said *Sit on my right hand* to one only, the Son named in the verses just before, so the one David bows to is no angel and no mere son of David, but the one the Father seats.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews asks which angel was ever told to sit at the right hand, so the one David bows to is no angel.

new_threads.title: Their city burned and the house left desolate
new_threads.summary_md:
It ain't new. A king sends servants with an invitation, the bidden seize them and kill them, and the king answers by burning their city. Yahusha (Jesus) tells it in the temple, and every piece of it was laid down before him.

*And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.* (Matthew 22:6)

*But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city.* (Matthew 22:7)

The ones who slew the servants are the rulers who killed the prophets, and he says so outright in the next chapter.

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37)

*Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.* (Matthew 23:38)

Jeremiah stood at the gate of the house in his own day and told the people what they were leaning on.

*Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), The temple of Yahuah (LORD), are these.* (Jeremiah 7:4)

Isaiah had shown that when Yahuah (the LORD) sends an army against a people, the army is his rod and not his equal.

*O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation.* (Isaiah 10:5)

Two chapters on, the disciples show him the buildings of the temple and he tells them what is coming.

*There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.* (Matthew 24:2)

What is judged in all of these is the house that was trusted for its own sake and the rulers who killed the ones sent to them. In the same sentence that leaves the house empty he speaks of gathering the children.
